ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, officers, controlling shareholders and UBOs against the following at incorporation and on an ongoing basis: Canada's sanctions lists (Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions, Global Affairs Canada consolidated sanctions list under the Special Economic Measures Act and the United Nations Act); the Criminal Code listed entities; FINTRAC PEV/PEP indicators as set out in the PCMLTFA regulations; and when the entity will use U.S. payment rails or have U.S. nexus, the OFAC SDN List and FATF high-risk / non-cooperative jurisdiction list. Enhanced due diligence is required for any PEP, sanctioned jurisdiction, or complex cross-border ownership structure; a risk-based compliance program must be documented prior to corporate filing.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta) - Name Search and Name Request through authorized Corporate Registry service providers; for federal incorporation: Corporations Canada's NUANS preliminary name search
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A corporate legal name must be expressed in English or French, or in a bilingual combination, using Latin-alphabet characters and including a mandatory legal element ('Ltd.', 'Inc.', 'Corp.', 'Ltee' or similar). Names in non-Latin scripts (e.g., Chinese characters) may be adopted as an additional 'name in another language' but will not be reflected on the Certificate of Incorporation in that script; the official legal name must be transliterated into Latin characters. The proposed name must be distinguishable from all existing corporate, trademark, and business names in Alberta and cannot be likely to deceive or mislead the public.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the proposed name is rejected by the Alberta Corporate Registry, the applicant may submit a written reconsideration request to the Director of Corporate Registry within 30 days of the rejection notice, providing evidence of distinguishability and justifying the requested name. If the Director upholds the rejection, the applicant may appeal to the Court of King's Bench of Alberta under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta). For a federal incorporation, a rejected NUANS name report may be appealed in writing to Corporations Canada for redetermination under the Canada Business Corporations Act; if denied, a further judicial review application may be filed in the Federal Court of Canada.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Generally permissible for a registered office, provided the address is a physical street address within Alberta and is not solely a post office box. A virtual office or registered agent service is acceptable for corporate registration for a cross-border e-commerce dietary supplement seller. However, if the entity obtains a Health Canada Natural Product Number (NPN) or a Natural Health Product Site Licence, or if it registers under the Alberta Pharmacy and Drug Act or Health Professions Act, the competent regulator may require an actual physical establishment address and may treat a virtual office as insufficient for the commercial substance requirements of the industry.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate-to-elevated: approximately 30% likelihood of an unannounced physical inspection within the first 24 months for a high-risk cross-border nutraceutical e-commerce business, based on Health Canada and Alberta regulator risk tiering; likelihood rises to 60-70% if the business holds a Natural Health Product Site Licence subject to Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP) inspections. FINTRAC AML compliance examinations are also conducted by risk tier, with a 15-20% annual probability for a high-risk merchant category.

incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital required; share subscriptions at par value permitted without escrow unless articles specify otherwise
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the sole incorporator subscribes for the initial share capital of the Corporation as set forth in the Articles of Incorporation, specifically [insert number] shares of the common shares class at a subscription price of $1 per share for a total subscription of $[insert amount]; RESOLVED that the registered office of the Corporation shall be established at [insert full address including street, city, province Alberta, postal code]; RESOLVED that [insert director name 1] be appointed as the first President and Chief Executive Officer, [insert director name 2] as the first Secretary, [insert director name 3] as the first Treasurer, and [insert director name 4] as the first Director of the Corporation; RESOLVED FURTHER that the Corporation's initial by-laws be adopted in the form presented to this meeting and that all actions taken by the incorporator prior to this meeting be ratified and confirmed. This resolution is passed on [insert date].

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access the Alberta Corporate Registry website portal, verify name availability through the search function, submit a formal name reservation application including the proposed name and incorporator information, and remit the applicable fee to secure the reservation for 90 days.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If name unavailable, select alternate name and reapply or proceed to incorporation using the reserved name

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare Articles of Incorporation on the prescribed form detailing share structure, directors, registered office, and incorporator; electronically or by mail submit with supporting documents and filing fee; include director consents where required.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If queried for deficiencies, cure within the specified period or resubmit corrected application

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, receive Certificate of Incorporation electronically or by mail; update corporate records with the Registry; file any required notices and appoint officers to commence operations.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If rejected, correct issues and refile or appeal through the Corporate Registry process

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No manufacturing or processing activities conducted; retail operations exempt from EIA. General compliance required for waste disposal, no hazardous emissions, and environmental protection standards

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) via My Business Account portal at canada.ca/revenue-agency
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Canadian corporations obtain Business Number (BN) through CRA online application using incorporation certificate and articles of association; foreign entities register similarly but must provide foreign incorporation documents and beneficial ownership information, with additional due diligence under Income Tax Act sections 116 and 218.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box elections available; taxation follows default entity-level rules under the Income Tax Act with provincial variations in Alberta.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Electronic filing of GST returns via CRA My Account; no real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping mandated for standard operations.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Suppliers of goods exported from Canada may claim zero-rating for GST on qualifying exports; offshore services may qualify under specific export criteria including proof of non-residency of recipient and payment receipt.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration, Bill of Lading, Inward Remittance Certificate
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Willful false statements or fraudulent zero-rating claims attract penalties under Excise Tax Act including fines, interest, and potential imprisonment for evasion.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada operates a free current account convertibility regime under IMF Article VIII. Capital account transactions are largely liberalized, permitting unrestricted repatriation of corporate profits, dividends, and equity investments for Canadian-incorporated entities. Profit remittance requires only standard corporate documentation, tax filings, and beneficial ownership disclosure; no surrender obligations or quantitative restrictions apply to legitimate business remittances.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canadian exporters are not subject to mandatory surrender of foreign exchange proceeds. Receipts must be reported to the Bank of Canada through the Electronic Data Interchange Reporting System (EDIR) within 30 days if exceeding CAD 50,000. Transactions occur at prevailing market rates with no statutory conversion ratios; compliance centers on accurate valuation and timely reporting.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium feasibility. Offshore digital EMIs face significant legal constraints under FINTRAC AML obligations and Alberta-specific health product regulations. High-risk merchant accounts for dietary supplements require enhanced due diligence, provincial licensing where applicable, and compliance with Health Canada Natural Health Product rules; many fintech providers impose geographic or product restrictions.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote corporate onboarding is permitted for Alberta entities with verified corporate documents, articles of incorporation, and director resolutions. Directors or authorized signers may be required to complete video KYC or in-person verification based on risk scoring; physical appearance is not universally mandated but enhanced scrutiny applies to high-risk online retail operations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk merchant account for dietary supplements and nutraceuticals
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Health Canada Natural Product Number (NPN) or Site License, product safety certificates, business license, detailed transaction volume analysis, source-of-funds documentation, and beneficial ownership register

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border payment flows and capital injections
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Corporate shareholder resolutions, trade contracts, import/export invoices, proof of legitimate business purpose, and tax residency certificates

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound capital injections utilize SWIFT MT103 or CHIPS wires with purpose code 'CAP'. Verification requires corporate board resolution, shareholder agreement excerpts, tax identification numbers, and proof of equity contribution. Alberta entities must maintain compliance with the Alberta Corporate Registry for any capital adjustments.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements route through SWIFT MT103 for international wire transfers or Commercial Letters of Credit issued via correspondent banks. All disbursements require supporting documentation including commercial invoices, purchase orders, shipping documents, and proof of goods receipt. Purpose codes must reflect legitimate trade activity.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 calendar days after the anniversary of incorporation or date of registration in Alberta
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fee CAD 100; failure to file for two consecutive years renders the corporation subject to administrative strike-off by the Registrar

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory audit for distributing (public) corporations under ABCA s. 216; private non-distributing corporations may waive auditor appointment via unanimous shareholder consent under s. 218; no quantitative size threshold applies
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS (CPA Canada Handbook Part I) for publicly accountable enterprises; ASPE (Part II) for private enterprises, or IFRS at election

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Alberta corporate law requires maintenance of a Register of Individuals with Significant Control (ISC) and annual confirmation upon shareholder transfer or other changes; no standalone UBO filing to the Corporate Registry, but the register must be available for inspection and updates must be reflected in the annual return
